Case Study

Launching Maestro, Amazon's First AI Music Experience

When generative AI was reshaping the tech landscape, Amazon Music saw an opportunity to lead. I helped launch Maestro — the streaming industry's first AI-powered playlist generator in the U.S. — turning mood and imagination into music discovery and positioning Amazon Music as the category innovator.

The Situation

AI Was Reshaping Tech — But Streaming Hadn't Moved

In 2024, generative AI was rapidly reshaping the technology landscape, but consumer-facing applications in streaming music had yet to emerge. Amazon Music identified an opportunity to lead the category by introducing a product that would fundamentally change how listeners discover music.

  • 1
    No major streaming service had launched a consumer AI product. Despite AI dominating tech headlines, no competitor had delivered a customer-facing generative AI music experience in the United States.
  • 2
    The interaction model was entirely new. Maestro relied on natural language prompts instead of traditional playlist browsing — requiring customers to learn a completely new way to discover music.
  • 3
    Customer education was critical. The launch needed to spark curiosity, educate listeners on prompt-based discovery, and demonstrate the product's capabilities from day one.
  • 4
    Amazon Entertainment's first AI product launch. The stakes extended beyond music — this was a milestone for the entire Amazon Entertainment organization.
The Mandate
Launch the streaming industry's first AI-powered music discovery experience — and position Amazon Music as the innovation leader in the category.
The Approach

Discovery Powered by Emotion and Imagination

We built the launch strategy around a clear narrative: instead of searching by artist or genre, listeners could simply type how they were feeling and Maestro would generate a custom soundtrack in seconds. The go-to-market coordinated product, PR, marketing, and media into a unified launch.

01
Category-Defining Positioning
Framed Maestro as a new way to discover music through natural language prompts — turning mood, humor, and creativity into playlist inputs. Positioned Amazon Music as the first major streaming service to bring generative AI directly to listeners.
Go-to-Market Strategy →
02
Beta-Driven Rollout
Launched Maestro as Amazon Music's first public product beta, enabling the team to test customer behavior, iterate quickly based on real usage data, and build momentum before full global release.
Growth & Lifecycle Marketing →
03
PR-Led Innovation Narrative
Focused heavily on establishing Amazon Music as the streaming service bringing generative AI to listeners first. Drove coverage across Billboard, TechCrunch, Engadget, The Verge, Hypebot, and leading industry newsletters.
Integrated Marketing →
04
Customer Education Through Prompts
Campaign creative showcased examples of imaginative prompts to help users understand how to interact with the product. Messaging and creative were coordinated across owned channels, social, and product surfaces to spark experimentation.
Content & Creator Marketing →

Impact

From Product Launch to Category Creation

Maestro demonstrated how generative AI could fundamentally reshape music discovery. By launching the streaming industry's first AI-powered playlist creator in the United States, Amazon Music positioned itself as a technology innovator while establishing a new interaction model for how listeners find and experience music.

The product moved beyond traditional search and curation to offer something entirely new: discovery powered by emotion, creativity, and natural language — setting the standard for what AI-driven music experiences could look like.

🤖
Maestro established Amazon Music as the first major streaming service to bring generative AI directly to listeners — creating a new category for AI-powered music discovery that the industry has since followed.
